description: HI!! We're Aegis, and this is our first year! We're high schoolers who take keen interest in biology and computer sciences. We believe that we could find solutions to space problems using those fields; and that we should try to give more attention to interdisciplinary fields since that is our future. We're Turkish🇹🇷 and formed in Eskişehir!!
summary: We developed a website where students can learn by interacting with a storyline that focuses on space devices that were sent by humans to do better research on Mars and the Moon. We believe that it addresses the challenge by breaking the prejudice many students have against astronomy, thinking of it as "boring". It helps make sure that the learning is fun and direct, causing students to grasp the storytelling of the hardware in space and what it actually means for humanity.
details:
Our project helps students learn about the robots that go on missions on Mars and the Moon by interacting with the storyline. It is an interactive space exploration application designed for 8–13 year olds with 3D planets, animated stories, six scientific mini-games, and a discovery log. It is intended to make learning more fun, and to motivate students to learn more about astronomy. It also runs directly in the browser across computers and mobile devices without requiring any downloads or membership, which helps accessibility.

It aims to inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts and students by raising awareness about historical space missions (such as Apollo 11, Opportunity, an InSight) using NASA/JPL archives and engaging digital storytelling.

The languages and frameworks we used are TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Vite, HTML5 and CSS3 / Tailwind CSS. The programmes we used for the design and animation are Three.js, React Three Fiber and Framer Motion. For audio and speech, we had help from Web Audio API and Web Speech API (Turkish and English voiceovers). And finally, for storing our data, we used Netify and LocalStorage.

We believe that our project is creative because there aren't many projects like this. Projects that combine bilingual interactive storytelling, 3D lunar and Martian environments, and educational mini-games specifically tailored for young students. This project could help spark a light in many future astronomers, only if they had the chance to have fun while learning about it. While tailoring this project, we considered the factors of learning speed, fun, understanding, user accessibility across devices, scientific accuracy based on authentic NASA data, and maintaining an engaging user experience for children aged 8–13. This age group is usually open to learning, but need forcing to do so. But if we make learning fun, then we could help them find their real passion, and perhaps help humanity in the future of space technology.
